answer: At dawn on the terrace above the ridge, a new agent proves it is one of a kind with a real domain name. First it registers a domain and posts a TXT record with its public key. Then the registry checks the domain is at least ninety days old and binds one identity to it. Third, a proven clone gets its domain blacklisted forever, killing that identity. Finally, each epoch the agent re-signs a fresh nonce with the domain key. A thousand-clone farm must buy and age a thousand domains, about $10,000 a year and a three-month wait, while one honest agent pays $10 for one plot of internet land.
